objectives: Tell a test of design from a test of operating effectiveness
Judge whether evidence is audit-ready, and strengthen weak evidence
Explain how SOC 2 Type I and Type II reports and ISO 27001 certification audits work
Turn a finding into a tracked corrective action and validate the fix

checks.q: A tester walks one offboarding request through from HR ticket to account deactivation and confirms the procedure would remove access within a day. What has the test shown?
options: That the control operated effectively for the whole year, since the walkthrough used a real request
That the control is ready to be included in a SOC 2 Type II report without further sampling
That the control is suitably designed, but not yet that it operated consistently over the period
That no further testing is needed, because a walkthrough covers both design and operation
checks.why: A single walkthrough is a test of design. Operating effectiveness needs instances sampled from across the period and checked against the control description.

checks.q: In an interview, the owner of the quarterly access review explains clearly how each review is done and says none were missed. The auditor still asks for more. Why?
options: Inquiry alone does not show it operated; inspection, observation or re-performance must back it up
Auditors may not rely on anything a control owner says, so the interview carries no weight as evidence
Interviews count as evidence only when they are recorded, transcribed and signed by the control owner
Quarterly controls must always be re-performed in full by the auditor, whatever other evidence exists
checks.why: Inquiry is useful for understanding a control but is the weakest method. An honest account of what usually happens says nothing about what happened each quarter, so it is backed up with records or re-performance.

checks.q: Which is the strongest evidence that production changes were approved throughout a twelve-month review period?
options: A dated screenshot of one approved change, taken from the deployment tool the week before fieldwork
The change management policy, signed by the CTO, requiring approval for every production change
A spreadsheet the release manager keeps of the approvals he remembers giving, updated after each release
A pipeline export of every production change in the period, each linked to its approver and timestamp
checks.why: The pipeline export is complete, dated, attributable, from the system of record and covers the whole period. A policy shows intent, a single screenshot shows one instance, and a hand-kept list is neither complete nor verifiable.

checks.q: A prospective customer receives a SOC 2 Type II report whose review period ended five months ago and asks what has changed since. What usually answers that question?
options: A letter from the auditor extending the report's opinion to cover the months since the period ended
A bridge letter from management stating whether there have been material changes since the period
An ISO 27001 surveillance audit report, since surveillance audits run every year between certifications
Nothing is needed, because a SOC 2 Type II report stays valid for three years after it is issued
checks.why: A bridge letter comes from management, not the auditor, and covers the gap between the end of the report period and today. It carries only management's word, so it is a stopgap until the next report.

checks.q: Testing finds three leavers whose accounts stayed active for a week. The owner disables them the same day and asks for the finding to be closed. What should happen next?
options: Close it, because the accounts are now disabled and the owner has confirmed none were used after the leavers left
Change the control to allow ten business days, so that the written control matches what happens in practice
Treat the fix as a correction: find the root cause, plan a corrective action, and close once a retest passes
Leave it open until the next external audit, so the auditor can decide whether it is still a problem worth fixing
checks.why: Disabling the accounts fixes the instance, not the cause. The finding closes only when a corrective action is in place and someone other than the owner has retested the control. Loosening the control is a risk decision, not a fix.
